A motor-side torque quantity within about 7% of the measured motor torque, and demonstrably not the same signal. The six form one family, successive members differing in the fifth digit.
signals.evidence: All six agree with each other to five digits and with the gravity model 8784 at rest, but the offset from measured torque is +7% on ROB_1 and -6% on ROB_2 -- a real difference, not a scale factor. Under motion 1613/1614 follow joint 1 at 69-75% with adjusted R2 0.94.
signals.name: Torque, reference or delivered
signals.next_test: Command a torque step and compare lead and lag against 4002.
signals.open_question: Whether this is the torque reference or the delivered torque, and what separates the six copies.
signals.ruled_out: Not the gravity model: unlike 8784 they vary during a joint-1 sweep, which changes no gravity term.

signals.description: A twelve-slot block that is constant in every state, does not respond to motion, and differs between the two robots. Sits immediately below the frozen path-level TCP pose at 516-522 and behaves the same way.

signals.ruled_out: Not a live quantity of any kind: peak-to-peak is exactly zero under motion.

signals.description: Rectified DC bus voltage of a drive module. -Axis is ignored: all six axes of a robot are fed from one bus and read the same value. Choose the module with the mechanical unit -- the measured cell had drive_module_1 and drive_module_2, one per robot, so the unit ROB_1 read module 1 and ROB_2 module 2. Per-module, ESTABLISHED 2026-09-02 by the DC-link investigation: identical to 6 significant figures across axes 1, 2 and 3 of one robot, and read on ROB_1 and ROB_2 in the same stream to compare the two modules. Re-confirmed 2026-09-05 with a second client: the two mechanical units give stable, bit-identical, DIFFERENT values -- 15.935 vs 16.046 V unpowered, 362.73 vs 362.18 V energised -- which they could not if the mechanical unit were ignored.
signals.evidence: Byte-identical to each other. Read 356.7 V armed and stationary, sagging to 337-341 V under a six-axis load, and decaying exponentially with tau = 389 s after the contactor opens -- the behaviour of a capacitor bank, and the basis of the 2026-09-02 drive-module comparison.
signals.name: DC-link voltage
signals.ruled_out: Not axis-indexed: the apparent per-axis spread is ripple, and the axis model only fit it because six groups over twelve samples fit half of any variance for free.

signals.description: Ten quantities between 13 and 32 that are completely indifferent to load and drift slowly over tens of minutes. Quantised to exactly 1/33 of a unit, so an ADC reading.
signals.evidence: Measured across motors-off, armed-holding, 45 minutes of continuous six-axis motion on BOTH robots, and cool-down: every one moved by less than its own sample noise between states (8000 read 31.08 idle, 31.32 armed, 31.06 moving, 31.0 cooling). Over the 20-minute armed campaign they drifted monotonically upward -- 8000 from 30.99 to 32.25 -- and were back down an hour later.
signals.name: Slow environmental measurement

signals.open_question: Whether these are cabinet, drive or ambient temperatures, and why 8008 sits near 14 while the rest sit 23-32.
signals.ruled_out: Not motor temperature, current, or any load-derived quantity: 45 minutes of six-axis motion on two robots moved them by nothing. Not axis-indexed either: the apparent per-axis spread is that slow drift, sampled in axis order.
